prering.title: In FIR / FFT / SPM mode (linear phase), slight pre-ringing may occur before steep filters. It is usually so small that it is barely visible on the waterfall – this is normal.
decramp.note: Decramp x6 / x8: lows less accurate
decramp.noteTitle: With decramp x6 / x8 the very high internal sample rate (288 / 384 kHz) can make low-frequency filters deviate by a few tenths of a dB. At 44.1 / 48 kHz, x4 is enough for the highs and accurate.

imp.title: AutoEq & Profile Importer
imp.tabManual: Manual File / Text Import (Squiglink, REW, APO)
imp.searchPh: Type the model (e.g. HD 600, Sundara, Chu, XM4, DT 770, Zero:RED)...
imp.filterNote: Real-time filtering of results from the built-in index and community repositories:
imp.zeroDoubleText: The factory preamp value from the database is applied directly. The system does NOT subtract the boost compensation a second time!
imp.loadFile: Load a file from your computer (.txt / .csv):
imp.textPh:
Or paste the text here directly...
Preamp: -6.2 dB
Filter 1: ON PK Fc 65 Hz Gain 5.8 dB Q 1.41
Filter 2: ON PK Fc 120 Hz Gain -8.5 dB Q 4.20
Filter 3: ON HSC Fc 10000 Hz Gain 3.0 dB Q 0.71
imp.smart1: • If the file has a Preamp: exactly that value is used, no double subtraction!
imp.smart2: • If the file has no Preamp: it is calculated from the peak of the complete resulting EQ curve (including the sum of overlapping bands), with a small margin.
imp.smart3: • Limiter: switches on automatically with a negative preamp (-1.0 dB threshold, True Peak oversampling) and catches inter-sample peaks.
cf.title: Crossfeed Simulator (Bauer bs2b / Meier)
cf.desc: Removes the unnatural “inside the head” stereo isolation of headphones. It models the acoustic shadowing and delay of the head (ITD/ILD), so the music is heard in front of you, like from a real pair of studio monitors, rather than inside your ears.
cv.title: Convolver (Partitioned FIR Engine)
cv.sampleRoomTitle: Load a test room correction impulse
cv.sampleHpTitle: Load a test headphone HRIR impulse
cv.desc: Load the room correction WAV / IRS file exported from a room measurement (e.g. REW or Cavern QuickEQ) here. Convolution is performed by zita-convolver (as in EasyEffects).
cv.none: No impulse response loaded – browse a WAV/IRS file
lim.title: Limiter & True Peak Protection
lim.ovsTitle: Oversampling can be set in the Oversampling selector
lim.desc: Prevents boosts in the EQ or room correction from driving the DAC's analog reconstruction filter into digital clipping. The primary protection against clipping is a correct preamp (matched to the full EQ curve); the limiter is a safety net (it switches on automatically when a profile with a negative preamp is loaded) and is not a hearing protection device.
bass.desc: For smaller speakers and bass-light headphones: rather than simply raising the level (which would cause cone distortion and rattling), it generates harmonics that the brain decodes as the presence of the low fundamental.

wf.noWebgl: The 3D waterfall cannot be shown on this computer (no WebGL). Audio processing and all other settings work.
lim.armKeep: {state} ({ceil} dB, {os}; no negative preamp, state unchanged)

ver.mismatchTitle: The interface and engine versions differ: restart the engine or reinstall Aqulify.
engine.offlineTitle: Start the engine: on Linux systemctl --user start aqulify, on Windows Aqulify.exe
engine.analysisOnly: Analysis only: the DSP settings affect the sound after the Aqulify EQ APO plugin is installed.
engine.idleTitle: When playback pauses, Equalizer APO stops the audio stream and with it Aqulify’s processing. It starts again automatically when playback resumes; this is not an error.
engine.noDevice: No playback device is available (e.g. a disconnected sound card), so audio processing is not running. Reconnect the device or choose another one in the Windows sound settings.
engine.pluginNotLoaded: Audio processing is not running on “{device}”. If this is a new audio device (e.g. a USB sound card), enable Equalizer APO for it in its Configurator; if it appears after an update, restart the computer.
engine.apoOtherDevice: Audio is now playing on “{device}”, but Equalizer APO is not enabled for this device, so audio processing is not running (it worked on “{apoDevice}”). Enable this device in the Equalizer APO Configurator, or switch back to “{apoDevice}”.
engine.apoConfiguratorTitle: Tick this audio device in the list, then restart the computer when Equalizer APO asks.
engine.apoConfiguratorFailed: The Equalizer APO Configurator did not start (it needs administrator permission).
engine.macPermissionTitle: Aqulify needs permission to capture system audio: System Settings → Privacy & Security → Screen & System Audio Recording. Without it, Aqulify also works with the BlackHole 2ch virtual device.
engine.macNoSourceTitle: Before macOS 14.2, system audio needs the BlackHole 2ch virtual device (free, existential.audio/blackhole). Once it is installed, Aqulify starts using it automatically.
engine.macDeviceTitle: No usable output device was found, or it could not be started. Connect one or choose another.
preset.confirmDelete: Delete the "{name}" profile? (The current EQ settings will not change.)
mt.desc: Automatic, restrained sound enhancer: it analyses the recording being played and only corrects what is missing or disturbing (boxy low-mids, dull highs, out-of-phase bass, narrow mix). It does not make things louder and does not compress: the output loudness matches the input.
mt.noData: No data: turn on Magic Touch (the engine must be running; on Windows it works with the EQ APO plugin).
mt.collecting: Analysing… (the first decisions take a few seconds)

mt.valLowMid: excess {ex} dB → cut {cut} dB at {hz} Hz
ctl.magicAmountHint: 0 % = untouched signal; up to 100 % corrections stay within hard limits (see the Details). Above 100 %: “Bold” range with a stronger effect, audible on good recordings too.
